trajectory_summary: The call opens with friction that the rep defuses cleanly, moves through verify and qualifiers efficiently, and lands on a workable text-follow-up plan for the bill. The one soft spot is pacing during the live bill-capture attempt, where the rep let a stalled account-creation process run until the customer himself called for a more organized approach. The outcome is a real next step, but it is a callback/text-follow-up, not a locked appointment.
outcome_dispute: No appointment day/time was ever set on this call — the rep never reached button_up or appointment_set. The call ends with a promise to text and the customer sending a bill photo later, which is a callback/pending-information state, not a booked or tentative appointment. Any v1 tag of 'booked' or 'tentative' would be miscalled; the correct tag is callback (or no_appointment if no callback time was pinned down, which it wasn't).

primary_coaching_focus.quote: Yes. No problem. So what I can do is I can just send you a text message.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The call ends without any specific day/time for a callback or closer appointment, which is the single biggest gap on this call — everything upstream (intro repair, verify, bill attempt) was handled reasonably, but the call has no owned next step for the rep to follow through on.

key_moments.stewart_read: This isn't a hard 'not interested' but a contact-frequency complaint; the rep's immediate reframe to 'I just confirm the information' resolves it via action rather than argument, matching the protocol's spirit even though the trigger phrase differs.

key_moments.stewart_read: Customer gives an unverified, self-uncertain answer to the credit qualifier and explicitly invites the rep to check. The rep's 'I believe you' closes the loop without flagging the uncertainty anywhere, which is exactly the stated-vs-verified credit ambiguity the schema leaves open as a policy question for Kenny.

key_moments.quote: Well, I was just saying, so you should have an online account with Dominion that you could just log in to, like, on your phone or a computer, and it will tell you your kilowatt usage there as well.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep correctly tries the online-login path when the paper bill is unavailable, which is a reasonable first move. The gap is pacing: once it became apparent the customer had no existing Dominion account and was creating one live on the call, the rep did not recognize the stall and pivot within the schema's 2-minute time budget — nearly two minutes pass before the customer himself calls for a more organized approach.
